item.title: The App lifecycle
item.description:
Every humus application is a bedrock.App, and the root package’s humus.App is the lifecycle every humus app type is built on. It reads its settings, listens for signals, builds the user’s dependencies, runs one or more Services, shuts them down within a grace period, releases what was built, and turns the outcome into an exit status.

Most applications will not use humus.App directly. Each runtime package — REST, gRPC, jobs, queues — provides an App of its own, built on humus.App with that package’s defaults, and that is the API most users touch. Using humus.App directly, for example to run a REST API and a gRPC service in one process, is the advanced path. Read this page before taking it; read it, too, to understand what the App a runtime package builds for you does.

item.title: Testing a humus App
item.description:
A humus App runs whole inside a test. Two packages make that possible, and a whole-App test imports both:

  • bedrocktest supplies the process the App runs on: its arguments and environment, which the test sets, its output, which the test reads, and its signals, which the test sends. bedrocktest.Start runs an App on a new process and hands back the process and a channel for the App’s exit status.
  • humustest supplies what a humus App needs beyond the process: a Host, whose in-memory network the App listens on and the test dials, and whose filesystem is confined to the test’s own temp directory; a certificate authority, NewCA, generated for each test; and TestService, the contract every Service must pass.

The network opens no real socket and starts no goroutines, so the App runs in a testing/synctest bubble. It needs no real environment, no real time and no file outside the test’s temp directory.
